Leiden is an improved version of the [Louvain algorithm] [Blondel08]. 
It has been proposed for single-cell analysis by [Levine15] [Levine15]. 
This requires having ran `neighbors/find_neighbors` or `neighbors/bbknn` first.

[Blondel08]: Blondel et al. (2008), Fast unfolding of communities in large networks, J. Stat. Mech.  
[Levine15]: Levine et al. (2015), Data-Driven Phenotypic Dissection of AML Reveals Progenitor-like Cells that Correlate with Prognosis, Cell.  
[Traag18]: Traag et al. (2018), From Louvain to Leiden: guaranteeing well-connected communities arXiv.  
[Wolf18]: Wolf et al. (2018), Scanpy: large-scale single-cell gene expression data analysis, Genome Biology.  


::: {.ref-description}
[Blondel08]: Blondel et al. (2008), Fast unfolding of communities in large networks, J. Stat. Mech.

`--n_iterations`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
How many iterations of the Leiden clustering algorithm to perform.
When defined, positive values above 2 define the total number of iterations to perform.
When not set, the algorithm will run until it reaches its optimal clustering.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Min]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seed`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Fix the initialization of the optimization. Can be used to increase reproducibility.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--resolution`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
A parameter value controlling the coarseness of the clustering. Higher values lead to more clusters.
Multiple values will result in clustering being performed multiple times.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `double` [required]{.arg-required}

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_compression`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Compression format to use for the output AnnData and/or Mudata H5 files.
By default no compression is applied.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"gzip"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"gzip"`, `"lzf"`

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/cluster/leiden/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/cluster/leiden);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/cluster/leiden/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
